newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi urges Prodi to dump Marxists.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi urges Prodi to dump Marxists.

text.p: Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Tuesday his alliance would consider lending parliamentary support to a minority government in Italy if Prime Minister Romano Prodi broke with the hard left.
Berlusconi made his offer in a speech at the end of a debate in the lower Chamber of Deputies on plans to send an Italian-led security force to Albania.

The force was approved by the opposition and the centre-left coalition but a decision to vote 'no' by the Communist Refoundation party, which secures Prodi's lower house majority, has raised doubts about the governent's future.
"Take a decision...We are ready to make our contribution," Berlusconi said, adding his Freedom Alliance bloc was not interested in a place in the government.
Prodi is facing his toughest political challenge since taking office last May as a result of the Refoundation mutiny.
Political sources expect him to face a parliamentary confidence vote to determine whether his coalition's alliance with the hard left can continue.

The main party in the governing coalition, the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), has previously rejected the possibility of a minority government but smaller, centrist forces in the government have said it should be considered.
